subject: pacu fish
title: A Piranha Cousin With Human-Looking Teeth Keeps Turning Up in American Lakes

scenes.text: A fish with human-looking teeth keeps turning up in American lakes. It's a piranha's cousin.
The pacu. From the Amazon and Orinoco rivers. Up to three feet long and 44 pounds.
Its teeth are square and flat, like molars. It uses them to crush seeds and nuts that fall into the river. Mostly, it eats plants.
Yet pacus have been caught in at least 26 American states, from Michigan to Arizona to New Jersey.
They're aquarium pets. They outgrow the tank, and people tip them into the nearest lake. Three came out of one Michigan lake in a single week.
They can't survive a northern winter. But a nut-cracking jaw in the wrong river can still outcompete the fish that belong there.

description:
The pacu is a South American relative of the piranha with square, flat teeth that look oddly human. It uses them to crush seeds and nuts, and it mostly eats plants.
Pacus can reach about a metre and 20 kilograms. Released aquarium pets have been caught in at least 26 US states; in one week in 2016 three were pulled from Lake St. Clair, Michigan. They cannot survive cold winters, but where they persist they can outcompete native fish and spread parasites.
Have you ever seen a fish with teeth like this? Comment below.
first_comment: Pacus have also turned up in Denmark and in a lake near Yuma, Arizona. Biologists say they are a bigger threat to native fish than to swimmers. Which animal lookalike should we cover next?
